free_tier.stated: No free tier on the pricing page. The page prices rotating residential traffic from $0.55/GB (the 'Regular' tab) and sells first-recharge bundles from 5 GB at $6 to 500 GB at $350.
free_tier.notes: The vendor's forum posts mention a 500 MB trial redemption code; no first-party page read states it, so no trial is recorded.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address or a traffic quota, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a proxy session or a rented address, not stored bytes

egress.terms: Billed per GB of traffic: 'GB-based Billing', 'Unlimited Bandwidth & Concurrency', and 'No, your purchased traffic is valid indefinitely. The traffic plan only consumes the allocated traffic quota.'

interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 forward proxy (the pricing page lists 'Protocols: SOCKS5/HTTP(S)'); the home page lists APIs and SDKs for Python, Node.js, Puppeteer and Selenium. Sticky sessions of 1 to 180 minutes or a new IP on every request.
tooling: Any client that speaks an HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 proxy with a username and password or an allowlisted source address: curl -x, python requests, rclone --socks5, or a host-side hop for a runtime that cannot dial a proxy itself. The vendor offers an API and SDK examples; no client wrapper is needed.
chaining: A host-side hop dials the vendor's HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 endpoint with credentials; the upstream sees an address from the vendor's pool in place of the caller's address.

limits.value: billed per GB: 'Regular' tab from $0.55/GB; first-recharge bundles 5 GB $6, 20 GB $24, 50 GB $55, 200 GB $180, 500 GB $350; purchased traffic has no expiry

limits_note: The vendor states unlimited bandwidth and concurrency; the binding quantity is the purchased GB. The pool size (100M+ residential IPs, 3,635,214 daily IPs shown) is the vendor's claim and was not measured.
binding_note: Every byte through the pool is metered per GB, so the quota is the purchase size; no request-rate or per-IP limit is stated.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form asks for an email address, an emailed verification code and a password, with a Google sign-in alternative; no phone, card or identity document appears on it. Payment methods are shown as icons on the pricing page and were not readable.

reliability_note: The pricing page and the sign-up page answered 200; the shorter /signup path answered 404. The pool figures are vendor claims with no independent measurement. unverified (rung 5): whether the exits are registered to a residential ISP; no published address was looked up.
confidence_note: Price, billing unit, session rule and sign-up fields come from the vendor's own pages; the pool size and the residential claim are vendor statements.

evidence.proved: The 'Regular' residential tab starts at $0.55 per GB.

evidence.quote: No, your purchased traffic is valid indefinitely. The traffic plan only consumes the allocated traffic quota.
evidence.proved: Purchased traffic has no expiry; billing is per GB.

evidence.quote: proxy001 supports sticky IPs and rotating IPs. Sticky IPs: Supports setting the online time of an IP from (1-180) minutes.
evidence.proved: Sticky sessions last 1 to 180 minutes; rotating mode changes the IP on every request.

evidence.quote: Over 100 million residential lPs, city-level targeting, 99.8% connectivity, response time <0.3s.
evidence.proved: The vendor claims 100 million residential IPs with city-level targeting.
The sign-up form asks for an email address, a verification code and a password.

evidence.quote: Proxy001 recruits global resellers with two cooperation options: CDKey distribution and API sub-accounts.
evidence.proved: The vendor sells through CDKey distribution and API sub-accounts.
The shorter /signup path answers HTTP 404, as the note states.

notes: Named on a Chinese-language proxy forum with a 500 MB trial code and a $0.55/GB headline. The 711Proxy home page quotes the same $0.55/GB headline, a 100M+ pool and 200+ countries with the same wording; whether the two share a backend is unverified.

extras.rung_note: A rotating residential pool presents a different single address per request, which is rung 2; no registration class was checked.
